name: SikaGunite GP
paste:
SIKAGUNITE® GP: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: SikaGunite® GP, April 2023, Version 01.03 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/r/sikagunite-gp.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide SikaGunite® GP where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.03).
1.2 Product description. SikaGunite® GP is a cement-based, ready to use, one component mortar. It is applied by mechanical application on vertical and overhead surfaces using the dry spraying process, and can be used in civil or mining applications.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer.
    - Concrete repair of bridges, canals, sewer linings, sea walls, culverts and tunnels.
    - Pier and dock supports.
    - Sewage treatment plants.
    - Marine environments.
    - Retaining walls.
    - Protection of steel work.
    - Embankment protection and stabilisation.
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.6.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. SikaGunite® GP
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: One component Gunite dry spray applied repair mortar
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals / certificates.
    - AS4020:2018 Approved for Potable Water Applications.
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - AS4020:2018: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Approvals / Certificates (p.1).
    - AS 1478.2: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Compressive strength (p.2).
    - ASTM C348: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Tensile strength in flexure (p.2).
    - AS 1012.10: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Tensile strength (p.2).
    - EN 12617: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Restrained shrinkage / expansion (p.2).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Easy to use with the addition of potable water.
    - Economical.
    - High resistance to chloride and sulfates.
    - Excellent abrasion resistance.
    - Controlled shrinkage.
2.5 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Appearance and colour: Concrete grey (mixed)
    - Density: 2,080 kg/m³
2.6 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Maximum grain size: ~ 2mm
    - Tensile strength: ~ 6.0 MPa at 28 days (Indirect Tensile) (AS 1012.10)
    - Restrained shrinkage / expansion: ≥ 2.0 MPa at 84 days (EN 12617)
2.7 Compressive strength.
    | 1 day | ~ 20 MPa |
    | 7 days | ~ 50 MPa |
    | 28 days | ~ 70 MPa |
    Test method printed: (AS 1478.2-A:2005)
    Note printed: Material and curing conditions at 23°C / 50% r.h. Above results based on 50mm x 50mm cube @ 0.113 w/p ratio
2.8 Tensile strength in flexure.
    | 1 day | 6.0 MPa |
    | 7 days | 9.0 MPa |
    | 28 days | 11.0 MPa |
    Test method printed: (ASTM C348)
2.9 Electrical resistivity.
    | 28 days | ~ 89,000 Ω.cm |
    | 56 days | ~ 122,000 Ω.cm |
    | 90 days | ~ 148,000 Ω.cm |
    Test method printed: (FM 5-578)
    Note printed: 50mm Probe Spacing
2.10 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 20 kg bag and 1000kg bulk bags on request
    - Shelf life: 9 months from date of production
    - Storage conditions: Stored properly in original, unopened and undamaged packaging in dry conditions.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.03) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate quality / pre-treatment.
    - Precise and efficient surface preparation is essential to achieve the high bond qualities of Gunite.
    - All concrete, mortar and stone substrates must be sound, clean and free from oils, grease and surface contaminants. All loose materials and surface laitance must be removed. Grit or grit/water blasting or scabbling is recommended.
    - Just prior to application pre-wet and wash down the substrate with water and air pressure from the spraying machine, blowing off any excess surface water with oil free pressurised air before spraying.
3.3 Substrate quality / pre-treatment - Reinforcement Corrosion Protection.
    - Small amount of reinforcement. 24 hours before Gunite application, apply 2 coats of brush applied SikaTop-110 EpoCem to the prepared steel (refer to the SikaTop-110 EpoCem data sheet).
    - Large amount of reinforcement. 24 hours before Gunite application, apply 2 coats of SikaTop-110 EpoCem by spray equipment to the prepared steel (refer to the SikaTop-110 EpoCem data sheet).

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.03) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Consumption: Approx. 105 bags per m³
    - Yield: Approx. 9.52 litre per 20 kg bag
    - Layer thickness: 10 mm to 175 mm approximately
    - Initial set time: 70 - 80 minutes approx. @ W/P ratio of 0.113
    - Final set time: 90 - 120 minutes approx. @ W/P ratio of 0.113
4.3 Application. SikaGunite® GP can be applied dry spraying process. In the dry shot process, the nozzleman determines the water content of the mix and therefore the quality of the sprayed mortar. A lower water/powder ratio can result in too much dust and a higher water/powder ratio can give a flowing mortar that will slump off the substrate. For applications to vertical surfaces up to 175 mm maybe achievable with overhead repairs up to 150mm depending on water additon. After spraying immediately screed off and trowel.
4.4 Curing treatment. Proper curing procedures are important to ensure the durability and quality of the repair. To prevent surface cracking, cure the repair mortar using plastic sheets, wet hession, or curing compounds such as SikaCure.
4.5 Cleaning of equipment. Remove non hardened Gunite from tools and equipment with water. Hardened material can only be removed mechanically.
4.6 Limitations and important considerations.
    - Store SikaGunite-GP in dry conditions.
    - Use only potable water at the nozzle. Please consult with technical department, for any initial recom-mendation on required amount of water.
    - Never apply to dry substrates.
    - Minimum surface and ambient temperature of 4°C during application.
    - Minimum application thickness is 12 mm.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Conditions stated in the limitations. Also stated in the data sheet limitations (clause 4.6):
    - Minimum surface and ambient temperature of 4°C during application.
5.3 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Compressive strength: 1 day | ~ 20 MPa; 7 days | ~ 50 MPa; 28 days | ~ 70 MPa (AS 1478.2-A:2005)
    - Tensile strength in flexure: 1 day | 6.0 MPa; 7 days | 9.0 MPa; 28 days | 11.0 MPa (ASTM C348)
    - Tensile strength: ~ 6.0 MPa at 28 days (Indirect Tensile) (AS 1012.10)
    - Restrained shrinkage / expansion: ≥ 2.0 MPa at 84 days (EN 12617)
    - Electrical resistivity: 28 days | ~ 89,000 Ω.cm; 56 days | ~ 122,000 Ω.cm; 90 days | ~ 148,000 Ω.cm (FM 5-578)
5.4 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.5 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: SikaGunite® GP, April 2023, Version 01.03, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/r/sikagunite-gp.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS SikaGuniteÂ® GP, https://aus.sika.com/dam/dms/au01/k/sds-sikagunite-gp.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety.
    - Avoid contact with the skin.
    - Protective gloves and clothing are recommended when using this product.
    - A full Safety Data Sheet is available from Sika on request.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
